subject.title: Telegram: apiRoot local Bot API server receives updates but never dispatches to agent sessions

question: For Telegram local Bot API migration, should OpenClaw scope or invalidate update offsets when `apiRoot` changes, rely on doctor/docs for manual reset, or keep the current account/token-only watermark behavior?
rationale: Source inspection shows the failure shape, but changing persisted polling-state semantics and tolerating `400: Logged out` during migration are compatibility-sensitive runtime choices.

options.title: Endpoint-Aware Runtime Repair
options.body: Scope or invalidate Telegram update offsets on endpoint changes, add a narrowly tested logged-out cleanup tolerance, and require live local Bot API proof before closing this issue.

options.title: Doctor Or Docs Reset
options.body: Keep runtime offsets keyed by account/token and make `openclaw doctor --fix` or documentation the supported reset path for endpoint migration.

options.title: Operator-Managed Advanced Workflow
options.body: Leave the current behavior in place and document that local Bot API endpoint switches require manual offset cleanup and cooldown handling.

recommendation.title: Endpoint-Aware Runtime Repair
recommendation.body: Scope or invalidate Telegram update offsets on endpoint changes, add a narrowly tested logged-out cleanup tolerance, and require live local Bot API proof before closing this issue.

likelyOwner.reason: The current offset and polling startup paths plus recent ingress-spool recovery history point to this owner as the best routing candidate for the policy choice.
